chunks: And it has been narrated from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
"Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the Earth; a likeness of His Light is as a niche in which is a lamp."

So he replied: It is an example Allah has given for us. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imams, may Allah's blessings be upon them all, are the Signs of Allah and His miracles through which one is guided towards Divine Unity, towards the interests of Religion, towards Islamic laws, towards obligations and recommendations. And there is no power except with Allah, the Most High and Most Great.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq interpret the Verse of Light regarding the Prophet and the Imams?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interpreting the 'Verse of Light' (24:35) not merely as a metaphor for divine illumination, but as a specific reference to the Prophet and the Twelve Imams as the tangible 'signs' (ayat) of God. This exegesis underscores their role as the essential conduit for attaining Tawhid and understanding the practicalities of Sharia, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the Imams' infallible guidance. The narration concludes by linking this spiritual authority to the ultimate source of strength, 'La quwwata illa billah'.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. It had been related on the authority of al-Sadiq (AS) that he (AS) was asked about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
“Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the Earth; a likeness of His Light is as a niche in which is a lamp.”

So he (AS) replied: Allah has given an example for us. The Prophet (SA) and the Imams, may Allah bless them all, are the Signs of Allah through which He guides people towards Divine Unity, towards His Religion, towards Islamic law, and towards (religious) obligations and recommendations. There is no power except Allah, the Most High and Most Great.
